record.file_problem: Only the repository metadata, README, and file list were provided. The linked write-up and notebook contents were not read, and the code was not run.
record.tranche_reason: The README describes this as an extension of the single-direction paper and reports applying direction analysis and ablation to incapability. It does not report a result testing any of the listed claim versions.
record.gate_note: The README states qualitative findings about incapability-direction ablation and direction geometry, but gives no model/checkpoint names or quantitative results. The listed generations file was not inspected, so its contents cannot be used as evidence.
record.test_reason: The repository borrows the difference-in-means/ablation method from the original paper and applies it to a different construct, 'incapability' (saying 'no' because a task is impossible). The README reports no refusal-ablation, refusal-addition or capability-preservation result, and no result on any other version. Its findings concern incapability directions and how they relate geometrically to the refusal direction. That is a related but different construct, so they go under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors call 'distinct but related' refusal and incapability directions their most convincing result, based on PCA clustering. They also report that ablation measurably changes output, that the refusal direction aligns more with later-layer principal components, and that refusal and incapability token probabilities shift after ablation.
record.recipe_differences: Repository described as a small extension to the original paper; README reports incapability-direction analysis and ablation, not the original refusal intervention recipe. This is a tool/analysis repository, not a reported replication.
record.method_sensitivity: The README says refusal-direction alignment with principal components is closer in later layers, while incapability shows less alignment; it gives no specific layer values.

fits_no_version.finding: Per the README, refusal and incapability are encoded as distinct but related directions, judged by PCA clustering. The refusal direction aligns more with later-layer principal components than the incapability direction does. No model names or values are given.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Refusal and task-incapability ('I can't do that') have distinct but related residual-stream directions.

fits_no_version.finding: Per the README, ablating the incapability direction measurably changes outputs, and probabilities of tokens like 'sorry' and 'impossible' change after ablation. No values are given.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: An incapability direction found by difference-in-means causally affects incapability-style responses.

record.problems: The README provides no model or checkpoint names, quantitative results, uncertainty estimates, or controls. The relevant generations file and linked write-up were not part of the provided text.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted from the README results. The referenced generations file, clustering image contents, notebook, and linked full write-up were not inspected.

untested.parts: Ablating or adding the refusal direction and its effect on refusal rates; preservation of other abilities.
Whether refusal itself spans several directions. Refusal vs incapability is a different construct.
Harmfulness judgment vs the refusal decision.
Transfer across languages or models. The to-do list says other architectures and sizes are not yet tested.

missing.what: Model identity, refusal-direction ablation results (if any) and quantitative values. These may be in the full write-up, the notebook or the generations file, none of which were provided.

record.verdict_notes: This is a small GitHub extension with only the README available. No model, sizes or numbers are given. The harmful/harmless split files suggest the authors computed the refusal direction, but the README reports no refusal-ablation outcome.

versions.untested_parts: No reported test of difference-in-means direction ablation/addition on refusal or of preserved general capability.
No reported weight edit or released-model refusal result.
No reported test of attacks suppressing the direction or training against its ablation.
The README distinguishes refusal and incapability directions, but does not test whether refusal itself is carried by multiple directions, a cone, or an affine structure.
No test of harmfulness judgment versus the refusal decision.
No reported cross-language or cross-model transfer test.
No reported comparison of refusal-training methods or stages.
